newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scandal could spur redebate on Hebron - Israeli.
newsitem.headline: Scandal could spur redebate on Hebron - Israeli.

text.p: Allegations of corruption in the appointment of an Israeli attorney general could result in the cabinet holding another debate on a pact with the PLO on last week's pullout from Hebron, a key lawmaker has said.

Israeli police are to decide on Sunday whether to probe charges that Aryeh Deri, leader of the Shas party, a coalition partner of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, conditioned his party's support of the hard-won Hebron accord on the appointment of lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney general.

State-owned television has alleged that Deri, an ultra-Orthodox ex-minister on trial since 1993 on a range of corruption charges, had won a promise from Bar-On of a plea bargain that would let Deri continue his political career.

Legislator Shaul Yahalom of the National Religious Party, which strongly opposed the U.S.-brokered pullout, told army radio in remarks broadcast on Saturday that if the reports proved true: "We will do everything we can to return the (Hebron) decision for a renewed (cabinet) discussion. That is clear."

Ending months of rancourous debate both with the Palestinians and within Netanyahu's cabinet, Israeli ministers voted 11 to 7 last week to approve the handover of 80 percent of the West Bank city to Yasser Arafat's PLO.
The partial withdrawal, carried out the next day, left 20,000 Palestinians in an Israeli-controlled sector where some 400 Jewish settlers and students live in the heart of violence-plagued Hebron.
The agreement includes Israeli pledges for additional troop withdrawals in the West Bank in the course of the year.
Two weeks ago Bar-On resigned within 12 hours of taking office, after criticism he was appointed more for his loyalty to Netanyahu's ruling Likud than for his legal acumen.
Netanyahu has called for a "quick and thorough" police investigation into allegations of Deri's reported involvement.

On Friday, the television said Netanyahu "was not in on the secret" of the plea bargain deal. Bar-On, Deri and Netanyahu have all denied the television charges. Deri has said he welcomes a police investigation.
Political analysts said that if allegations against Deri are proven, the affair could result in the downfall of the Netanyahu government.
Trade and Industry Minister Natan Sharansky has been quoted as saying that "if there is 10 percent truth to the television's story there is no room for the government to continue its term."
